subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept core, default-off model-mediated writes to SOUL.md, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces?
rationale: The requested behavior is missing and well-scoped, but it adds durable writes to a prompt-loaded instruction file plus new config, CLI, and tool surfaces that require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Accept guarded core contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses private gating, respects send policy, provides visible notice and undo, and proves hostile-input handling.

options.title: Move to memory or plugin seam
options.body: Reject direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for durable preference capture through memory plugins or a new plugin/API extension.

options.title: Decline automatic mutation
options.body: Close the SOUL auto-evolution direction if maintainers do not want model-mediated instruction-file writes at all.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses private gating, respects send policy, provides visible notice and undo, and proves hostile-input handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, core/plugin boundaries, and security posture, and this handle is tied to those architecture and template histories.
